memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites celebrated the Passover. The day after the Passover, that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain. The manna stopped the day after they ate this food from the land; there was no longer any manna for the Israelites, but that year they ate the produce of Canaan. — Josh 5:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two significant things happen together here. First, Israel celebrates the Passover in the Promised Land — the feast that remembered how God delivered them from Egypt by the blood of the lamb. Even as they stand on the brink of a new chapter, they pause to remember the great salvation that first made them God's people. Fresh beginnings are built on remembering God's saving grace.

Second, the manna stops. For forty years God had faithfully sent bread from heaven each morning. Now that they can eat the produce of the land, the manna ceases. Notice: God's provision changed form, but it never failed. In the wilderness He provided manna; in the land He provided crops. God does not always provide in the same way, but He always provides. When one form of His supply ends, another begins.

This can comfort us when a familiar source of provision dries up. God is not limited to one method. He may close one door of provision precisely because He is opening another.

The Passover points us straight to Christ, "our Passover lamb" who has been sacrificed for us (1 Cor 5:7). And the manna points to Him too, for Jesus said, "I am the bread of life" (John 6:35). Whether in wilderness seasons or seasons of plenty, He is the true and lasting sustenance our souls need. His provision never runs out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you pause to remember God's saving grace even as you step into new seasons?
2. Has God ever changed the way He provides for you, without ever failing to provide?
3. How does Jesus, the true bread of life, sustain you in every season?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your provision never fails, even when it changes form. Help me feed on Christ, the true bread of life, in every season. Amen.
